paragraphs: Yud Keret: Kiddushin 16b, ‘Rav Yosef said: I see Yud Keret here’—that is, he made a great city out of a small yod. The Arukh explains that it is a sage’s name. In the margin of the new Talmud edition, a gaon explains that Yud Keret is a town’s name, like Rabbi Yose of Yudkeret. In Chiddushei Ritva there, Rashi’s reading is ‘Rav Yosef said: I see Yud Keret here’; his explanation is that this tanna needlessly prolonged his words and makes a great city out of a small yod. But Raavad reads ‘Rabbah said: I see Yud Keret here,’ and it is the name of a very harsh man who did not spare even his children, as related in Taanit about Rabbi Yose of Yukrat. They brought him here by analogy, to say that this too is a harsh objection. This is more correct. End quotation.
